statement: Solve $4\sin^{3}\theta-3\sin\theta=-\tfrac12$ for $0\le \theta\le \pi$, and state how many solutions there are.
solution: Since $\sin 3\theta=3\sin\theta-4\sin^{3}\theta$, the equation becomes $-\sin 3\theta=-\tfrac12$, i.e. $\sin 3\theta=\tfrac12$. For $3\theta\in[0,3\pi]$ this gives $3\theta=\tfrac{\pi}{6},\tfrac{5\pi}{6},\tfrac{13\pi}{6},\tfrac{17\pi}{6}$. Hence $\theta=\tfrac{\pi}{18},\tfrac{5\pi}{18},\tfrac{13\pi}{18},\tfrac{17\pi}{18}$ — four solutions in $[0,\pi]$.
